nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Powers the algae, seagrass and mangroves of the shallow, sunlit waters and tidal flats around the islands.

nodes.name: Tides
nodes.desc: Big tides flood and drain the mangroves and mudflats twice a day, carrying nutrients in and moving food around for crabs, fish and wading birds.

nodes.name: Mud and nutrients
nodes.desc: Intertidal mud holds the nutrients that mangroves, seagrass and algae use, and is where much dead matter ends up.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Bacteria and fungi break down mangrove leaves, dead algae and carcasses, returning nutrients to the mud.

nodes.name: Mangroves
nodes.desc: Tidal forest that makes up large areas of the islands. A Wikipedia page on a park there says mangroves help molluscs, fish and sea turtles breed.

nodes.name: Seagrass
nodes.desc: Underwater meadows in shallow lagoons and bays, grazed by green turtles and, in places, manatees.

nodes.name: Microalgae and phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny algae in the water and on mudflats. They feed zooplankton, crabs and grazing fish.

nodes.name: Coastal grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses on shores and clearings that hippos graze after leaving the water at night.

nodes.name: Oil palm
nodes.desc: Common on the islands. Its fruit is a main food for palm-nut vultures.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny drifting grazers of phytoplankton that feed on algae and in turn feed small fish.

nodes.name: Fiddler crab
nodes.desc: Burrowing crab of muddy shores that sifts algae and detritus from sediment. Wading birds feed on crabs like it.

nodes.name: Flathead grey mullet
nodes.desc: Coastal fish that grazes algae and detritus on mud and sand, a staple prey of inshore dolphins.

nodes.name: Green sea turtle
nodes.desc: Adults graze mainly seagrasses and algae. Tiger sharks are their main predator.

nodes.name: West African manatee
nodes.desc: Eats plants growing on or over the water. In estuaries it feeds on mangrove foliage. Guinea-Bissau is among the countries with most manatees.

nodes.name: Hippopotamus
nodes.desc: Rests in water and comes ashore at night to graze grass. Its carcasses feed vultures.

nodes.name: Bar-tailed godwit
nodes.desc: Migrant wader that winters on African coasts, probing mud for worms, small shellfish and crustaceans.

nodes.name: Atlantic humpback dolphin
nodes.desc: Lives in shallow coastal and estuarine water and mainly eats inshore schooling fish such as mullet.

nodes.name: Osprey
nodes.desc: Fish-eating raptor that dives for fish in coastal waters; recorded often in the area.

nodes.name: Palm-nut vulture
nodes.desc: Eats mostly oil-palm fruit, plus crabs, fish and carrion. Common in coastal forests and mangrove swamps.

nodes.name: Hooded vulture
nodes.desc: Small scavenging vulture; GloBI records it feeding on hippo carcasses.

nodes.name: Tiger shark
nodes.desc: Main predator of adult green turtles, often hunting near nesting beaches.
